rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card and predictions before data; synthetic validation (N = 4 on #4/#6 schedules, N = 21 on #51's, plus a dense control world); 9 closed-roster N = 4 units on two clocks with day bootstraps, a shift null and held-out log-likelihood; natives N1 and N2; 238 estimates rows; confirm.py frozen and dry-run (not run). One amendment (A1, stratified variants) after the synthetic, before real data.
rationale.faithfulness: The HH's 10% claim fails (1/9 units), but the failure is understood and predicted by the synthetic: persistence (J_ii) breaks TAP and MS, and the law held in 9/9 real units. Couplings themselves are at noise level, which limits the benchmark. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E0 F2 G1 H1 I1.
rationale.usefulness: A method rule for the project and for anyone fitting kinetic Ising models to agent logs: report J_ii; above ~0.6 use exact or pseudo-likelihood, not TAP/MS; naive MF underestimates couplings by 5-55%.

one_line: Mean-field inversions match exact kinetic Ising ML only when agents' own states are not persistent (1/9 real N = 4 units; TAP 0.05, MS 0.03); with J_ii 0.86-1.22 TAP has no solution on 25-75% of rows, MS overshoots up to x3.8 and naive MF shrinks couplings (median error 0.25); same law in synthetic N = 4 and N = 21 worlds.

models.note: exact ML fine; mean-field inversions fail under own-state persistence

v2.claim: Mean-field inversions (TAP, Sessak–Monasson, naive) match exact kinetic-Ising ML only when agents' self-coupling is weak (J_ii ≤ 0.6, 1/9 units); with persistent own states TAP fails on 25–75% of rows, MS overestimates couplings up to ×3.8 and naive MF underestimates (shrink 0.45–0.95), as synthetic worlds at N = 4 and 21 predicted before data

ladder.factor: mechanism predicted by the synthetic before real data, held 9/9
carries to N = 21 (best method agrees 15/16 cells)
penalty: off-diagonal ML couplings at noise level in 7/9

v2.decision: fit agent couplings by exact (pseudo-)likelihood, not mean-field inversions, whenever agents' own states persist
